# Details

## Script information

In this notebook, we continue after the data processing (`01_processing_all_gating.qmd`) and cover the downstream analysis that follows for the data group that includes the **t0/t1** subset of the data. This includes:

-   Perform analyses focused on CAR-T cells before (t0) and after (t1) infusion
-   Address questions related to: a) How do CAR-T cells react upon infusion (t1 vs t0), and b) how do CAR-T cells behave as compared to normal T cells (FMC63+ vs FMC63- cells)?

\

## Study and experimental outline

Study led by Prof. Suzuki Yutaka and Dr. Kashima Yukie (Tokyo University, Japan). Samples collected from three donors (32, 44, 50) that have received CAR-T treatment. The CAR-T product was analyzed before infusion, and thereafter, PBMC samples were collected days post infusion (DPI) (8-9, 13, and 24 days).

Here, we will focus on the CAR-T product and 8-9 dpi samples.

```{r echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warnings=FALSE, results='asis'}
sample_table <- "
|  Sample ID    |  Donor ID   | Sample type  | DPI  |
|:-------------:|:-----------:|:------------:|:----:|
| TKB_CAR_T_64  | 32          | CAR-T prod.  |  --  |
| TKB_CAR_T_73  | 32          | PBMC         |  d8  |
| TKB_CAR_T_95  | 44          | CAR-T prod.  |  --  |
| TKB_CAR_T_97  | 44          | PBMC         |  d8  |
| TKB_CAR_T_105 | 50          | CAR-T prod.  |  --  |
| TKB_CAR_T_112 | 50          | PBMC         |  d9  |
"
cat(sample_table)
```

# Analysis

For this analysis we are focusing on the t0 and t1 samples, meaning that we are in particular looking at the CAR-T cells and how they were affected by infusion across all three donors.

For this downstream analysis we will aim to cover:

-   Differential abundance analysis between CAR+ T cells before/after infusion, looking at CD4 and CD8 populations separately. We can use CAR- T cells comparison results as "control".
-   Protein spatial polarization scores in each population, before/after infusion. "Raw" and differential scores. Specifically look at FMC63 polarity.
-   Protein spatial colocalization scores in each population, before/after infusion. "Raw" and differential scores.
-   Cell layout visualizations of FMC63

Potential analysis: - Patch detection: Look for B cell patches on CAR+T cells (should not be there before infusion(?), hopefully detectable after infusion - but perhaps too few B cells in donors overall to even cause trogocytosis?)

### Population refinement

#### Density scatter plots

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
DefaultAssay(data_t0t1) <- "mpxCells"
celltypes_plot <- grep("CD", data_t0t1$celltype |> unique(), value = T)
markers_plot <- c("CD4", "CD8", "FMC63")

p_list <- lapply(markers_plot, function(m) {
  p <- DensityScatterPlot(
    subset(data_t0t1, celltype %in% celltypes_plot),
    pt_size = 0.5,
    layer = "data",
    marker1 = "CD3E",
    marker2 = m,
    facet_vars = "celltype"
  ) &
    geom_hline(yintercept = 1.75, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey")
  return(p)
})
p_list[[4]] <- DensityScatterPlot(
  subset(data_t0t1, celltype %in% celltypes_plot),
  pt_size = 0.5,
  layer = "data",
  marker1 = "CD4",
  marker2 = "CD8",
  facet_vars = "celltype"
) &
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.75, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey")

p <- Reduce("|", p_list) &
  theme_linedraw() &
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank())
p

pdf(
  here("results", "analysis_t0t1", "abundance_tcell_markers_density_plot.pdf"),
  width = 10,
  height = 7
)
p
dev.off()
```

### Protein abundance in CD8 FMC63+ T cells (T0) 

Look at proteins across the CD8 FMC63+ T cell populations in t0 between donors. Identify markers based on average CLR.


```{r}
DefaultAssay(data_t0t1) <- "mpxCells"
samples_plot <- mdat_df |> filter(timepoint == "t0") |> pull(sample) |> unique()
ct <- "CD8 T FMC63+"
```

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=3}
markers_all <- rownames(data_t0t1)
cd8_cart_t0_abundance <- data_t0t1 %>%
  subset(celltype == ct & sample %in% samples_plot) |>
  FetchData(
    vars = c("donor", markers_all),
    assay = "mpxCells",
    layer = "data"
  ) %>%
  group_by(donor) %>%
  summarise_at(c(markers_all), mean, na.rm = TRUE)

markers_mean <- cd8_cart_t0_abundance |>
  summarise_at(c(markers_all), mean, na.rm = TRUE)
markers_keep <- names(markers_mean)[markers_mean > 0]

cd8_cart_t0_abundance_filt <- cd8_cart_t0_abundance[, c(
  "donor",
  markers_keep
)] |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  column_to_rownames("donor")

lims <- c(0, 5)
p <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
  cd8_cart_t0_abundance_filt,
  cellwidth = 14,
  cellheight = 14,
  fontsize = 12,
  cluster_rows = F,
  treeheight_col = 10,
  treeheight_row = 10,
  border_color = "white",
  border_width = 0.001,
  breaks = seq(lims[1], lims[2], 0.1),
  color = viridis::mako(length(seq(lims[1], lims[2], 0.1)), direction = -1),
  # color = cherry_gradient(length(seq(lims[1], lims[2], 0.1))),
  main = "Protein abundance in FMC63+ CD8 T cells (t0)\n"
)
p

pdf(
  here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "abundance_cd8_cart_t0_expressed_proteins.pdf"
  ),
  width = 10,
  height = 3
)
p
dev.off()
```

### Differential abundance

```{r}
groups_test <- c("CD4 T FMC63+", "CD4 T", "CD8 T FMC63+", "CD8 T")

#' Prepare data
dat_test <- data_t0t1 |>
  subset(celltype %in% groups_test)

#' Collect info about number of cells per group
daa_cell_stats <- dat_test[[]] |>
  rename(celltype = "celltype") |>
  group_by(celltype, donor, timepoint) |>
  summarize(n_cells = n())
```

#### Comparing t1 vs t0

```{r}
#' Run differential abundance test
daa_res <- RunDAA(
  dat_test,
  contrast_column = "timepoint",
  reference = "t0",
  targets = "t1",
  group_vars = "celltype"
)

daa_res <- daa_res |>
  rename(celltype = "celltype") |>
  relocate(celltype) |>
  relocate(difference, .before = p)
```

```{r}
#' View results
display_dt(daa_res, rownames = FALSE)
```

#### Comparing CAR+ vs CAR-

```{r}
#' Run differential abundance test
daa_res_car <- RunDAA(
  dat_test,
  contrast_column = "FMC63_status_clr",
  reference = "FMC63-",
  targets = "FMC63+",
  group_vars = c("celltype_broad", "timepoint")
)

daa_res_car <- daa_res_car |>
  rename(celltype = "celltype_broad") |>
  relocate(timepoint) |>
  relocate(celltype) |>
  relocate(difference, .before = p)
```

```{r}
#' View results
display_dt(daa_res_car, rownames = FALSE)
```

Next, let's explore the significantly abundant proteins.

We can start by looking at the number of differentially abundant proteins, and do this per cell type.

\

#### Comparing t1 vs t0

```{r}
daa_res <- daa_res |>
  mutate(sign = ifelse(p_adj < 0.01, "sign.", "n.s"))

daa_res_sign <- daa_res |>
  filter(p_adj < 0.01)
```

```{r}
dap_list <- daa_res_sign |>
  group_by(celltype) |>
  group_map(~ .x$marker)

names(dap_list) <- daa_res_sign$celltype |> unique()

dap_list
```

\
**Volcano**

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
p <- ggplot(daa_res, aes(x = difference, y = -log10(p_adj), color = sign)) + # , color = difference
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("grey80", "black")) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(-1, 1), col = "grey") +
  facet_wrap(~celltype, scales = "free_y") +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(1.1 * min(daa_res$difference), 1.1 * max(daa_res$difference))
  ) +
  theme_linedraw() +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = ifelse(abs(difference) > 1, as.character(marker), '')),
    hjust = -0.2,
    vjust = 0
  ) +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "none",
    axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 12)
  )
p

pdf(
  here("results", "analysis_t0t1", "abundance_daa_vulcano_tcells_t1t0.pdf"),
  width = 10,
  height = 8
)
p
dev.off()
```

*Positive values: higher abundance in t1 compared to t0. Significant values at an adj. p \< 0.01 shown in black, n.s in grey.*

\

Here we can see that most differential proteins are either shared or unique to the CAR- T cell population, while there are actually only a few proteins that are specifically associated to being differentially abundant in the CAR+ T cells. Let's look closer at which these proteins are.

```{r}
car_unique <- list(
  CAR_CD4T = dap_list[[2]][!dap_list[[2]] %in% dap_list[[1]]],
  CAR_CD8T = dap_list[[4]][!dap_list[[4]] %in% dap_list[[3]]]
)

car_unique
```

**Unique markers -- Heatmaps**

We can have a look at these proteins and visualize their values across the different samples.

```{r fig.width=6, fig.height=3}
markers_select <- car_unique |> unlist() |> unique()
lim_break <- 1.5
daa_res_sign %>%
  filter(marker %in% markers_select) |>
  # mutate(difference = ifelse(p_adj>0.01, 0, difference)) |>
  select(difference, celltype, marker) %>%
  tidyr::unite("population", celltype, sep = " ") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = "population", values_from = "difference") %>%
  column_to_rownames("marker") %>%
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>%
  clipr::write_clip(allow_non_interactive = TRUE) |>
  t() |>
  pheatmap::pheatmap(
    cellwidth = 14,
    cellheight = 14,
    fontsize = 12,
    cluster_rows = F,
    treeheight_col = 10,
    breaks = seq(-lim_break, lim_break, 0.1),
    color = differential_pal(length(seq(-lim_break, lim_break, 0.1))),
    border_color = "white",
    border_width = 0.001,
    width = 12
  ) -> daa_hm
daa_hm

pdf(
  here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "abundance_daa_heatmap_meandiff_tcells_t1t0.pdf"
  ),
  width = 6,
  height = 3
)
daa_hm
dev.off()
```

*Differential abundance results using Wilcoxon rank sum test. Color scale: Mean abundance difference.*

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=3}
  # mutate(difference = ifelse(p_adj>0.01, 0, difference)) |>
  select(difference, celltype, marker) %>%
  tidyr::unite("population", celltype, sep = " ") |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = "population", values_from = "difference") %>%
  column_to_rownames("marker") %>%
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>%
  clipr::write_clip(allow_non_interactive = TRUE) |>
  t() |>
  pheatmap::pheatmap(
    cellwidth = 14,
    cellheight = 14,
    fontsize = 12,
    cluster_rows = F,
    treeheight_col = 10,
    breaks = seq(-lim_break, lim_break, 0.1),
    color = differential_pal(length(seq(-lim_break, lim_break, 0.1))),
    border_color = "white",
    border_width = 0.001,
    width = 12
  ) -> daa_hm
daa_hm

pdf(
  here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "abundance_daa_heatmap_meandiff_tcells_t1t0_CD8Tmarkers.pdf"
  ),
  width = 14,
  height = 3
)
daa_hm
dev.off()
```

*Differential abundance results using Wilcoxon rank sum test. Color scale: Mean abundance difference.*

## Spatial: Polarization

-   Protein spatial polarization scores in each population, before/after infusion. "Raw" and differential scores. Specifically look at FMC63 polarity.

For the next part, we will look at polarization scores across our selected populations. Thereafter, we'll look at differential polarization scores between t1 vs t0 and FMC63+ vs FMC63-.

### Prepare data

We will start to fetch the polarization score data and filter it to exclude low abundance markers.

```{r}
#' Fetch data
data_t0t1_prox <- data_t0t1
data_t0t1_prox$component <- NULL

polscores_dat <- PolarizationScores(
  data_t0t1_prox,
  meta_data_columns = c(
    "sample",
    "FMC63_status_clr",
    "celltype_broad",
    "celltype",
    "timepoint"
  )
)
polscores_dat$celltype_timepoint <- paste0(
  polscores_dat$celltype_broad,
  "_",
  polscores_dat$timepoint
)
```

```{r}
#' Filter data - apply a strict filter on protein abundance
cts <- data_t0t1_prox %>%
  JoinLayers() %>%
  LayerData(layer = "counts") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("marker") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-marker, names_to = "component", values_to = "counts")

polscores_dat <- polscores_dat %>%
  left_join(cts) %>%
  rename(marker_count = counts)
```

```{r fig.width=3, fig.height=3}
boxplot(log2(polscores_dat$marker_count))
length(polscores_dat$marker_count)
boxplot(log2(polscores_dat$marker_count[polscores_dat$marker_count > 20]))
length(polscores_dat$marker_count[polscores_dat$marker_count > 20])
boxplot(log2(polscores_dat$marker_count[polscores_dat$marker_count > 50]))
length(polscores_dat$marker_count[polscores_dat$marker_count > 50])
```

```{r}
#' Filter
count_cutoff <- 50
polscores_dat_filt <- polscores_dat %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  filter(marker_count > count_cutoff)
```

### Differential analysis

For the differential analysis, we want to filter the data a bit further to ensure that the proteins we test are present in a higher number of cells per cell type.

```{r}
DefaultAssay(data_t0t1) <- "mpxCells"
data_t0t1 <- PolarizationScoresToAssay(data_t0t1)
DefaultAssay(data_t0t1) <- "polarization"

n_cells_min <- 20
# sample_cell_n <- data_t0t1_prox[[]] |>
#   group_by(celltype) |>
#   summarize(n())

polscores_dat_filt2 <- polscores_dat_filt |>
  group_by(marker, timepoint, celltype) %>%
  filter(n() > n_cells_min)
```

```{r}
# Filter markers - keep only those that are present in both conditions
keep_markers <- polscores_dat_filt2 %>%
  select(marker, celltype, timepoint) %>%
  unique() %>%
  group_by(marker, celltype) %>%
  summarise(n = n()) %>%
  filter(n == 2) %>%
  pull(marker) |>
  unique()
```

\

#### Comparing t1 vs t0

```{r}
#| warning: false
pol_res <- RunDPA(
  polscores_dat_filt2 |>
    filter(marker %in% keep_markers) |>
    filter(celltype_broad %in% c("CD4 T", "CD8 T")),
  contrast_column = "timepoint",
  reference = "t0",
  targets = "t1",
  group_vars = "celltype"
)

pol_res <- pol_res |>
  rename(celltype = "celltype") |>
  relocate(celltype) |>
  relocate(marker, .before = estimate) |>
  relocate(p, .after = estimate) |>
  relocate(p_adj, .after = p)
```

```{r}
write.csv(
  pol_res,
  file = here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "polarity_dpa_res_timepoint_tcells.csv"
  ),
  row.names = F
)
```

View all results:

```{r}
#' View results
display_dt(pol_res, rownames = FALSE, rows_per_page = 5)
```

Look at only significant findings:

```{r}
#' View results
display_dt(pol_res |> filter(p_adj < 0.05), rownames = FALSE)
```

Here we identify quite a large number of significantly differentially polarized proteins when comparing states before and after infusion. For instance, we find FMC63, which show a lowered polarization in the CAR+ T cells after infusion compared to before.

\

#### Comparing CAR+ vs CAR-

```{r}
#| warning: false
pol_res_car <- RunDPA(
  polscores_dat_filt2 |>
    filter(marker %in% keep_markers) |>
    filter(celltype_broad %in% c("CD4 T", "CD8 T")),
  contrast_column = "FMC63_status_clr",
  reference = "FMC63-",
  targets = "FMC63+",
  group_vars = c("celltype_broad", "timepoint")
)

pol_res_car <- pol_res_car |>
  rename(celltype = "celltype_broad") |>
  relocate(celltype) |>
  relocate(marker, .before = estimate) |>
  relocate(p, .after = estimate) |>
  relocate(p_adj, .after = p)
```

```{r}
write.csv(
  pol_res_car,
  file = here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "polarity_dpa_res_fmcstatus_tcells.csv"
  ),
  row.names = F
)
```

View all results:

```{r}
#' View results
display_dt(pol_res_car, rownames = FALSE, rows_per_page = 5)
```

Look at only significant findings:

```{r}
#' View results
display_dt(pol_res_car |> filter(p_adj < 0.05), rownames = FALSE)
```

Here we see that very few proteins were robustly identified to be differently polarized between CAR+ vs CAR- T cells. The two interesting findings here relate to CD45, which is more polarized in FMC63+ CD4 T cells before infusion, and CD45RA, which is less polarized in FMA63+ CD8 T cells after infusion. CD45 is an important protein for T cell activation while CD45RA is a marker of naive T cells.

## Spatial: Colocalization

Next, we'll do the same as the polarization analysis but for the colocalization data.

### Prepare data

We will start to fetch the colocalization score data and filter it to exclude low abundance markers.

```{r}
#' Fetch data
# data_t0t1_prox <- data_t0t1
# data_t0t1_prox$component <- NULL

colocscores_dat <- ColocalizationScores(
  data_t0t1_prox,
  meta_data_columns = c(
    "sample",
    "donor",
    "FMC63_status_clr",
    "celltype_broad",
    "celltype",
    "timepoint"
  )
)

colocscores_dat$celltype_timepoint <- paste0(
  colocscores_dat$celltype_broad,
  "_",
  colocscores_dat$timepoint
)
```

```{r}
#' Fetch marker count data
cts <- data_t0t1_prox %>%
  JoinLayers() %>%
  LayerData(layer = "counts") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  tibble::rownames_to_column("marker") %>%
  tidyr::pivot_longer(-marker, names_to = "component", values_to = "counts")

# Add counts info to the colocalization scores
colocscores_dat_filt <- colocscores_dat %>%
  left_join(cts, by = c("marker_1" = "marker", "component")) %>%
  rename(marker_1_count = counts) %>%
  left_join(cts, by = c("marker_2" = "marker", "component")) %>%
  rename(marker_2_count = counts) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(lower_marker_count = min(marker_1_count, marker_2_count))
```

```{r}
#' Filter to only retain marker pairs where the lowest abundant marker has an abundance
#' higher than 20 or the maximum isotype control abundance (whichever is higher)
count_cutoff <- 50
colocscores_dat_filt <- colocscores_dat_filt %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  filter(lower_marker_count > count_cutoff)
```

```{r fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
#' View the filtered colocalization score data
colocscores_dat_filt %>%
  group_by(marker_1, marker_2) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), median = median(pearson_z)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = median)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(50, 100), linetype = "dashed", color = "orange") +
  xlab("count_of_expressing_cells") +
  ylab("pearson_z_median") +
  ggtitle("Colocalization Scores") +
  theme_bw()
```

```{r}
#' Filter data to exclude markers with very low component detection rate in samples.
#' We can set this to 50, which will exclude the marker pairs with the dominating variability in colocalization scores
n_cell_cutoff <- 50
colocscores_dat_filt <- colocscores_dat_filt %>%
  group_by(marker_1, marker_2, sample) %>%
  filter(n() >= n_cell_cutoff)
```

```{r fig.width=6, fig.height=4}
#' View the filtered colocalization score data
colocscores_dat_filt %>%
  group_by(marker_1, marker_2) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), median = median(pearson_z)) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = n, y = median)) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(50), linetype = "dashed", color = "orange") +
  xlab("count_of_expressing_cells") +
  ylab("pearson_z_median") +
  ggtitle("Colocalization Scores - Filtered data") +
  theme_bw()
```

\

### Visualize raw scores

#### Overall scores per donor, timepoint, and T cell

Let's start by just looking at the overall colocalization patterns we have in the samples and cell types of interest.

```{r}
#' Prepare colocalization score data for running `SummarizeProximityScores()`
colocscores_dat_filt_test <- colocscores_dat_filt
colocscores_dat_filt_test$join_count_z <- colocscores_dat_filt_test$pearson_z
```

To begin, we summarize the colocalization scores for every sample and cell type, which will allow us to study the colocalization patterns across donors and timepoints.

```{r}
colocscores_summarized <- SummarizeProximityScores(
  colocscores_dat_filt_test,
  group_vars = c("sample", "celltype"),
  proximity_metric = "join_count_z",
  summary_stat = "mean",
  include_missing_obs = T
)

colocscores_summarized <- colocscores_summarized |>
  rename(celltype = celltype) |>
  merge(mdat_df, by = "sample") |>
  as_tibble()
```

```{r fig.width=20, fig.height=30}
#' Generate raw summarized colocalization score heatmaps for all samples and cell types
samples_plot <- colocscores_summarized$sample |> unique()
celltypes_plot <- colocscores_summarized$celltype |> unique()
celltypes_plot <- grep("CD", celltypes_plot, value = T) |> sort()

p_list_cells <- lapply(celltypes_plot, function(ct) {
  p_samples <- lapply(samples_plot, function(sample_select) {
    donor <- mdat_df |> filter(sample == sample_select) |> pull(donor)
    tp <- mdat_df |> filter(sample == sample_select) |> pull(timepoint)
    hm_title <- paste0(ct, " (", donor, ", ", tp, ")")
    p <- ColocalizationHeatmap(
      colocscores_summarized |> filter(celltype == ct, sample == sample_select),
      value_col = "mean_join_count_z",
      # size_col = "pct_detected",
      type = "tile",
      legend_title = "Mean\npearson Z",
      legend_range = c(-10, 10),
      treeheight_row = 20,
      treeheight_col = 20,
      main = hm_title
    )
    return(p |> ggplotify::as.ggplot())
  })
  p_grid <- wrap_plots(p_samples, ncol = 2)
  return(p_grid)
})
names(p_list_cells) <- p_list_cells
for (p in p_list_cells) {
  print(p)
}

pdf(
  here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "colocalization_raw_summarized_scores_per_sample_tcell_equal.pdf"
  ),
  width = 20,
  height = 30
)
for (p in p_list_cells) {
  print(p)
}
dev.off()
```

\

#### Filtered scores per donor, timepoint, and T cell

Let's do the same visualizations, but put to the same color scale and in the same marker order, for easier comparison.

```{r fig.width=20, fig.height=30}
#' Generate raw summarized colocalization score heatmaps for all samples and cell types
samples_plot <- colocscores_summarized$sample |> unique()
celltypes_plot <- colocscores_summarized$celltype |> unique()
celltypes_plot <- grep("CD", celltypes_plot, value = T) |> sort()

p_list_cells <- lapply(celltypes_plot, function(ct) {
  markers_shared <- colocscores_summarized |>
    filter(celltype == ct) |>
    mutate(marker_pair = paste0(marker_1, ":", marker_2)) |>
    group_by(sample) |>
    select(sample, marker_pair) |>
    group_map(~ .x$marker_pair) |>
    setNames(nm = samples_plot)
  markers_shared <- Reduce(intersect, markers_shared) |>
    strsplit(":") |>
    unlist() |>
    unique()
  markers_shared <- c(markers_shared, "FMC63")

  p_samples <- list()
  for (i in 1:length(samples_plot)) {
    sample_select <- samples_plot[i]
    donor <- mdat_df |> filter(sample == sample_select) |> pull(donor)
    tp <- mdat_df |> filter(sample == sample_select) |> pull(timepoint)
    hm_title <- paste0("\n", ct, " (", donor, ", ", tp, ")")

    if (i %in% c(1)) {
      # c(1, 3, 5)
      p <- ColocalizationHeatmap_custom(
        colocscores_summarized |>
          filter(marker_1 %in% markers_shared, marker_2 %in% markers_shared) |>
          filter(celltype == ct, sample == sample_select) |>
          mutate(size_same = ifelse(abs(mean_join_count_z) < 0.01, 0, 1)) |>
          mutate(
            size_diff_mean = ifelse(
              abs(mean_join_count_z) < 0.01,
              0,
              abs(mean_join_count_z)
            ),
            size_constant = 1
          ),
        value_col = "mean_join_count_z",
        size_col = "size_constant",
        type = "dots",
        legend_range = c(-5, 5),
        size_range = c(1, 5),
        legend_title = "Mean\npearson Z"
      ) &
        labs(title = hm_title, x = "", y = "")

      p_build <- ggplot2::ggplot_build(p)
      m_order <- p_build$layout$panel_params[[1]]$x$get_labels()
    } else {
      p <- ColocalizationHeatmap_custom(
        colocscores_summarized |>
          filter(celltype == ct, sample == sample_select) |>
          filter(marker_1 %in% m_order, marker_2 %in% m_order) |>
          mutate(size_same = ifelse(abs(mean_join_count_z) < 0.01, 0, 1)) |>
          mutate(
            size_diff_mean = ifelse(
              abs(mean_join_count_z) < 0.01,
              0,
              abs(mean_join_count_z)
            ),
            size_constant = 1
          ),
        value_col = "mean_join_count_z",
        size_col = "size_constant",
        type = "dots",
        legend_range = c(-5, 5),
        size_range = c(2, 5),
        marker_order = m_order,
        cluster_rows = F,
        cluster_cols = F,
        legend_title = "Mean\npearson Z"
      ) &
        labs(title = hm_title, x = "", y = "")
    }

    # return(p |> ggplotify::as.ggplot())
    p_samples[[i]] <- p
  }
  p_grid <- wrap_plots(p_samples, ncol = 2)
  return(
    p_grid &
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 0, vjust = 0)
      )
  )
})
names(p_list_cells) <- celltypes_plot

pdf(
  here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "colocalization_raw_summarized_scores_per_sample_tcell_dots_equal.pdf"
  ),
  width = 18,
  height = 20
)
for (p in p_list_cells) {
  print(p)
}
dev.off()
```

#### Summarized scores per timepoint and T cell

We can also summarize the colocalization data at just a cell type and per timepoint level. This summarizing is done on a cell-level (agnostic of donor origin), i.e. there might be imbalances driven based on cell frequencies between donors.

```{r}
colocscores_summarized_tp <- SummarizeProximityScores(
  colocscores_dat_filt_test,
  group_vars = c("timepoint", "celltype"),
  proximity_metric = "join_count_z",
  summary_stat = "mean",
  include_missing_obs = T
) |>
  rename(celltype = celltype)
```

```{r fig.width=20, fig.height=10}
#' Generate raw summarized colocalization score heatmaps for all samples and cell types

p_list_cells <- lapply(celltypes_plot, function(ct) {
  p_tp <- lapply(tp_plot, function(tp) {
    hm_title <- paste0(ct, " (", tp, ")")
    p <- ColocalizationHeatmap(
      colocscores_summarized_tp |> filter(celltype == ct, timepoint == tp),
      value_col = "mean_join_count_z",
      # size_col = "pct_detected",
      type = "tile",
      legend_title = "Mean\npearson Z",
      treeheight_row = 20,
      treeheight_col = 20,
      main = hm_title
    )
    return(p |> ggplotify::as.ggplot())
  })
  p_grid <- wrap_plots(p_tp, ncol = 2)
  return(p_grid)
})
```

### Differential analys

Next, we want to see if there are any significant protein colocalization differences that can be observed between e.g. CAR+ CD8 T cells before vs after infusion.

#### Comparing t1 vs t0

```{r}
#| warning: false
col_res <- RunDCA(
  colocscores_dat_filt |>
    filter(celltype_broad %in% c("CD4 T", "CD8 T")),
  contrast_column = "timepoint",
  reference = "t0",
  targets = "t1",
  group_vars = "celltype"
)

col_res <- col_res |>
  rename(celltype = "celltype") |>
  mutate(marker_pair = paste0(marker_1, ":", marker_2)) |>
  relocate(celltype) |>
  relocate(marker_pair, .before = estimate) |>
  relocate(p, .after = estimate) |>
  relocate(p_adj, .after = p)
```

```{r}
write.csv(
  col_res,
  file = here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "colocalization_dca_res_timepoint_tcells.csv"
  ),
  row.names = F
)
```

View all results:

```{r}
#' View results
display_dt(col_res, rownames = FALSE, rows_per_page = 5)
```

Look at only significant findings:

```{r}
#' View results
display_dt(
  col_res |> filter(p_adj < 0.01) |> arrange(-abs(estimate)),
  rownames = FALSE
)
```

### Visualize differential analysis

\

#### Comparing t1 vs t0

First, it'd be interesting to see which unique colocalization pairs we identify in CAR- and CAR+ T cells from each comparison.

```{r}
  filter(p_adj < 0.01)
```

Here, it seems like a CD82 is colocalizing more with various other proteins when the CD8 CAR-T cells are infused as compared to their state before infusion. From the proximity data, we could however see that CD82 was being less polarized after infusion. For instance, we see CD82 colocalizing (more) strongly with CD8. A very strong segregation between CD82:CD45 is seen both at t0 and t1, after infusion they segregate a lot less than before. Similarly, but reversed, is the B2M:HLA-ABC (HLA class I) colocalization, which is seen to be strong in both time points but to a much lesser degree after the infusion of the CD8 CAR-T cells.

```{r}
#' Let's create a function for repeating the same plot
plot_coloc_network <- function(
  coloc_score_data,
  markers_plot,
  cap_values = FALSE,
  coloc_cap = NA
) {
  #' Prepare data
  df_net <- coloc_score_data %>%
    filter(celltype == "CD8 T FMC63+") |>
    filter(marker_1 %in% markers_plot & marker_2 %in% markers_plot) %>%
    select(marker_1, marker_2, pearson_z, component, timepoint) %>%
    group_by(timepoint, marker_1, marker_2) %>%
    summarize(average_coloc = mean(pearson_z)) %>%
    mutate(from = marker_1, to = marker_2)

  #' Include this is you want to cap the highest/lowest values in the visualization to a set value
  if (cap_values) {
    if (!is.na(coloc_cap)) {
      coloc_cap <- coloc_cap
    }
    df_net <- df_net |>
      mutate(
        average_coloc = case_when(
          average_coloc > coloc_cap ~ coloc_cap,
          average_coloc < -coloc_cap ~ -coloc_cap,
          TRUE ~ average_coloc
        )
      )
  }

  #' Plot graph
  p <- tidygraph::as_tbl_graph(df_net) %>%
    ggraph(layout = "kk") +
    geom_edge_link(
      aes(
        color = average_coloc
        # width = abs(average_coloc)
      ),
      width = 5
    ) +
    geom_node_label(
      aes(label = name),
      size = 4
    ) +
    scale_edge_color_gradientn(
      colours = c("#728BB1", "white", "#CD6F8D"),
      limits = c(
        -abs(max(df_net$average_coloc)),
        abs(max(df_net$average_coloc))
      )
    ) +
    facet_edges(~timepoint, nrow = 1) +
    labs(title = "FMC63+ CD8 T cell") +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme(
      aspect.ratio = 1,
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 12, vjust = 4, face = "bold"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
      panel.spacing = unit(3, "lines")
    )
  p
  return(p)
}
```

```{r fig.width=10, fig.height=3}

  colocscores_dat,
  markers_plot = c("CD45", "CD44", "CD18", "CD11a")
)

)

)

)
```

```{r}
#' Let's make a new updated function for making the new colocalization networks
plot_coloc_network_v2 <- function(
  coloc_score_data,
  markers_plot,
  cap_values = FALSE,
  coloc_cap = NA
) {
  #' Prepare data
  df_net <- coloc_score_data %>%
    filter(celltype_broad == "CD8 T", timepoint == "t1") |>
    filter(marker_1 %in% markers_plot & marker_2 %in% markers_plot) %>%
    select(marker_1, marker_2, pearson_z, component, FMC63_status_clr) %>%
    group_by(FMC63_status_clr, marker_1, marker_2) %>%
    summarize(average_coloc = mean(pearson_z)) %>%
    mutate(from = marker_1, to = marker_2)

  #' Include this is you want to cap the highest/lowest values in the visualization to a set value
  if (cap_values) {
    if (!is.na(coloc_cap)) {
      coloc_cap <- coloc_cap
    }
    df_net <- df_net |>
      mutate(
        average_coloc = case_when(
          average_coloc > coloc_cap ~ coloc_cap,
          average_coloc < -coloc_cap ~ -coloc_cap,
          TRUE ~ average_coloc
        )
      )
  }

  #' Plot graph
  p <- tidygraph::as_tbl_graph(df_net) %>%
    ggraph(layout = "kk") +
    geom_edge_link(
      aes(
        color = average_coloc
        # width = abs(average_coloc)
      ),
      width = 5
    ) +
    geom_node_label(
      aes(label = name),
      size = 4
    ) +
    scale_edge_color_gradientn(
      colours = c("#728BB1", "white", "#CD6F8D"),
      limits = c(
        -abs(max(df_net$average_coloc)),
        abs(max(df_net$average_coloc))
      )
    ) +
    facet_edges(~FMC63_status_clr, nrow = 1) +
    labs(title = "CD8 T cells at t1") +
    coord_cartesian(clip = "off") +
    theme(
      aspect.ratio = 1,
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = NA),
      strip.text = element_text(size = 12, vjust = 4, face = "bold"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white"),
      panel.spacing = unit(3, "lines")
    )
  p
  return(p)
}
```

```{r fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = "bold"
      )
    ) +
    guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3)))

  p <- p1 / p2

  return(p)
})
```

```{r}
  filter(celltype == celltype_select) |>

  mutate(marker_other = ifelse(marker_1 == "FMC63", marker_2, marker_1))

fmc_coloc_dat |>
  distinct(sample, donor, timepoint, n_cells)
```
\

Identify markers with same colocalization score directionality in two (or three) donors: 

```{r}
fmc_marker_coloc <- fmc_coloc_dat |>
  filter(mean_join_count_z > 0) |>
  group_by(marker_other, timepoint) |>
  summarize(n = n()) |>
  filter(n > 1) |> # Check that more than 2 donors show consistent patterns
  arrange(timepoint) |>
  group_by(timepoint) |>
  group_map(~ .x$marker_other) |>
  setNames(c("t0", "t1"))

fmc_marker_coloc
```
```{r}
fmc_marker_segregate <- fmc_coloc_dat |>
  filter(mean_join_count_z < 0) |>
  group_by(marker_other, timepoint) |>
  summarize(n = n()) |>
  filter(n > 1) |> # Check that more than 2 donors show consistent patterns
  arrange(timepoint) |>
  group_by(timepoint) |>
  group_map(~ .x$marker_other) |>
  setNames(c("t0", "t1"))

fmc_marker_segregate
```


#### Heatmap (FMC63+ CD8+ T cells)

Make heatmap of FMC63 colocalization partners using colocalization scores for the different donors and timepoints.

```{r}
#' Select markers to plot
markers_plot_up <- c("FMC63", unlist(fmc_marker_coloc) |> unique())
markers_plot_down <- c("FMC63", unlist(fmc_marker_segregate) |> unique())
markers_plot <- c(markers_plot_up, markers_plot_down) |> unique()

#' Cells to plot
comp_plot <- colocscores_dat_filt %>%
  filter(celltype == "CD8 T FMC63+") |>
  mutate(dtp = paste(donor, timepoint)) |>
  filter(dtp != "donor_44 t1") |>
  pull(component)


#' Filter markers to plot based on ensuring they have enough abundance in both t0 and t1
#' Here we can set a cutoff on average CLR values
DefaultAssay(data_t0t1) <- "mpxCells"
markers_plot_filt <- data_t0t1 %>%
  subset(celltype == "CD8 T FMC63+") |>
  subset(cells = unique(comp_plot)) |>
  FetchData(
    vars = c("timepoint", markers_plot),
    assay = "mpxCells",
    layer = "data"
  ) %>%
  group_by(timepoint) %>%
  summarise_at(c(markers_plot), mean, na.rm = TRUE) |>
  summarise_at(c(markers_plot), min, na.rm = TRUE) |>
  # summarise_at(c(markers_plot), mean, na.rm = TRUE) |>
  t() |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  rownames_to_column("marker") |>
  filter(V1 > 0) |>
  pull(marker)

DefaultAssay(data_t0t1) <- "polarization"
```

```{r fig.width=6, fig.height=12}
#' Prepare data
hm_dat <- colocscores_dat_filt %>%
  filter(celltype == "CD8 T FMC63+") |>
  filter(marker_1 == "FMC63" | marker_2 == "FMC63") |>
  mutate(marker_other = ifelse(marker_1 == "FMC63", marker_2, marker_1)) |>
  filter(marker_other %in% markers_plot & marker_other %in% markers_plot) %>%
  select(
    marker_1,
    marker_2,
    marker_other,
    pearson_z,
    component,
    donor,
    timepoint
  ) %>%
  # mutate(marker_pair = paste0(marker_1, ":", marker_2)) |>
  mutate(marker_pair = paste0("FMC63", ":", marker_other)) |>
  group_by(donor, timepoint, marker_pair) %>%
  summarize(average_coloc = mean(pearson_z)) |>
  mutate(sample_time = paste0(donor, "_", timepoint)) |>
  filter(sample_time != "donor_44_t1") |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(sample_time, marker_pair, average_coloc) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = marker_pair, values_from = average_coloc) %>%
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>%
  as.data.frame() |>
  column_to_rownames("sample_time") |>
```

```{r fig.width=6, fig.height=10}
  filter(celltype == "CD8 T FMC63+") |>
  filter(marker_1 == "FMC63" | marker_2 == "FMC63") |>
  mutate(marker_other = ifelse(marker_1 == "FMC63", marker_2, marker_1)) |>
  filter(
    marker_other %in% markers_plot_filt & marker_other %in% markers_plot_filt
  ) %>%
  select(
    marker_1,
    marker_2,
    marker_other,
    pearson_z,
    component,
    donor,
    timepoint
  ) %>%
  mutate(marker_pair = paste0(marker_other, ":", "FMC63")) |>
  group_by(donor, timepoint, marker_pair) %>%
  summarize(average_coloc = mean(pearson_z)) |>
  mutate(sample_time = paste0(donor, "_", timepoint)) |>
  filter(sample_time != "donor_44_t1") |>
  ungroup() |>
  select(sample_time, marker_pair, average_coloc) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = marker_pair, values_from = average_coloc) %>%
  replace(is.na(.), 0) %>%
  as.data.frame() |>
  column_to_rownames("sample_time") |>
  t() %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  filter(abs(rowMeans(select_if(., is.numeric), na.rm = TRUE)) > 0) # Adjust here to change if pairs should be further filtered

annotation_col <- mdat_df |>
  mutate(sample_time = paste0(donor, "_", timepoint)) |>
  select(sample_time, donor, timepoint) |>
  distinct() |>
  as.tibble() |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  column_to_rownames("sample_time")

col_order <- annotation_col |>
  arrange(timepoint, donor) |>
  rownames() |>
  intersect(colnames(hm_dat))
hm_dat <- hm_dat[, col_order]

lim_break <- 4
fmc_hm <- pheatmap::pheatmap(
  hm_dat,
  cellwidth = 14,
  cellheight = 14,
  fontsize = 12,
  treeheight_col = 10,
  treeheight_row = 10,
  cluster_cols = F,
  border_color = "white",
  na_col = "grey90",
  border_width = 0.001,
  breaks = seq(-lim_break, lim_break, 0.1),
  color = differential_pal(length(seq(-lim_break, lim_break, 0.1))),
  annotation_colors = ann_colors,
  annotation_col = annotation_col,
  main = "CAR colocalization partners\nin FMC63+ CD8 T cells"
)
fmc_hm

pdf(
  here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "colocalization_raw_fmc63_centered_heatmap_filteredCLR.pdf"
  ),
  width = 6,
  height = 10
)
fmc_hm
dev.off()
```

## Cell visualizations

Generate cell graph visualizations of the highlighted polarized proteins and FMC63.

### FMC63 in CD8 T cells at t0 and t1

To make figures of the individual cell graphs, we first want to limit the dataset and select which cells to look at. E.g. for looking at FMC63, we want to ensure we look at cells that represents cells with a high FMC63 polarization.

```{r}
# polscores_dat_filt$celltype_timepoint |> unique()
# polscores_dat_filt$celltype |> unique()

components_select_fmc <- polscores_dat_filt |>
  filter(
    celltype == "CD8 T FMC63+",
    marker == "FMC63",
    morans_p_adjusted < 0.01, # Keep only significantly polarized components
    marker_count > 100 # Keep only components with a high marker count
  ) |>
  group_by(timepoint) |>
  slice_max(order_by = morans_z, n = 15) |>
  pull(component) |>
  unique()

data_cell_plot <- data_t0t1 |> subset(cells = components_select_fmc)

DefaultAssay(data_cell_plot) <- "mpxCells"
data_cell_plot <- data_cell_plot |> subset(CD4 < 0) # Some doublets were still detected(!) despite the new gating. Setting a CLR cutoff at 0 helped remove these components.

components_select_fmc
```

```{r}
DensityScatterPlot(
  data_cell_plot,
  pt_size = 0.5,
  layer = "data",
  marker1 = "CD8",
  marker2 = "CD4",
  facet_vars = "celltype"
) &
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1.75, linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey")
```

Here we can see that some components have obtained a very strange looking layout. We want to avoid visualizing these components, so we can remove them from the next visualization.

```{r}
components_rm <- c(
  "TKB_CAR_T_95_3258c468268f4ca7",
  "TKB_CAR-T_73_d69c244bfb6f8688",
  "TKB_CAR_T_112_7079fa0b0fa19fb6"
)
```

Let's start by visualizing FMC63 for all selected cells at t0 (before infusion).

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
components_plot <- data_cell_plot[[]] |>
  filter(!component %in% components_rm) |>
  filter(timepoint == "t0") |>
  pull(component)

p <- Plot2DGraph(
  data_cell_plot,
  cells = components_plot,
  layout_method = "wpmds",
  marker = "FMC63",
  colors = cherry_gradient(11),
  node_size = 0.5,
  collect_scales = F
) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 3) &
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
p

pdf(
  here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "cell_layout_cd8_cart_cells_fmc63_t0_top_cells.pdf"
  ),
  width = 14,
  height = 8
)
p
dev.off()
```

Here we can see quite nicely that FMC63 appears to polarize to one or two foci of the cell surface for most/all of the selected components.

Let's see if the same is seen for the t1 components selected.

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=8}
components_plot <- data_cell_plot[[]] |>
  filter(!component %in% components_rm) |>
  filter(timepoint == "t1") |>
  pull(component)

p <- Plot2DGraph(
  data_cell_plot,
  cells = components_plot,
  layout_method = "wpmds",
  marker = "FMC63",
  colors = cherry_gradient(11),
  node_size = 0.5,
  collect_scales = F
) +
  plot_layout(ncol = 4) &
  theme(plot.title = element_text(size = 11))
p

pdf(
  here(
    "results",
    "analysis_t0t1",
    "cell_layout_cd8_cart_cells_fmc63_t1_top_cells.pdf"
  ),
  width = 14,
  height = 8
)
p
dev.off()
```

As could be suspected from the FMC63 polarity scores, we do not see the same clear degree of spatial clustering or polarization of FMC63 in the cells after infusion. Good to bear in mind here, that the components selected were the ones with the highest scoring of FMC63 polarization.

Next, we can look pairwise at selected markers, and label based on donor and time point, to be able to compare the time point difference.

```{r}
components_plot <- data_cell_plot[[]] |>

  merge(score_info_add, by = "component") |>
  arrange(timepoint, -morans_z) |>
  group_by(timepoint, donor) |>
  slice_head(n = 2)

plot_titles <- setNames(

)
```

# Conclusion

In this notebook, we have covered the various comparisons of T cells in all donors at the time points before infusion (t0; CAR-T product alone) and after infusion (t1; CAR+/- T cells in PBMC at 8-9 dpi). We could detect several proteins displaying differential abundance, polarization, and colocalization patterns across the comparisons. Mainly, effects were observed in the CD8 T cells, and here we could identify a few patterns that related to FMC63 status and/or phenotype before vs after being infused in the patients.
